claims.claim_text: Transformer efficiency can be bounded by argument rather than looked up: assume a large unit is only 95 percent efficient, work out the resulting dissipation, and it becomes obvious the device would destroy itself — so real ones must be far above 99 percent.
claims.quote_verbatim: let's assume it's only 95% efficient transformer. What's the energy loss in that transformer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: Transformer losses appear as heat inside the windings, so an efficiency shortfall of even a few percent in a multi-megawatt unit melts the wire insulation and shorts the winding — the loss figure is a survival limit, not a running cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: would melt the insulation on the wires in the transformer. It would just melt and short out
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Proposals to drop solid-state transformers into existing distribution understate what they are replacing: conventional units run around 99 percent efficient and are extremely reliable, so a 96 percent solid-state substitute gives back several percent as heat across every megawatt that passes through it.
claims.quote_verbatim: are like 99% efficient and they're super reliable
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Alternating current was adopted for distribution because transformers make raising and lowering voltage easy; almost everything else about AC — reactive power in particular — is harder than the DC equivalent.
claims.quote_verbatim: the reason we use AC is basically because of transformers
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: High-voltage DC transmission has to convert at both ends and take the conversion losses, whereas AC transmission at 500 kV between major plants uses transformers that are already extremely efficient on generation that is already alternating — which is why the DC case has to be won on distance rather than on efficiency alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: transformers are massively efficient and you're generating AC anyway
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: The HVDC trade is explicit: accept conversion losses at each end in exchange for lower losses over the distance in between, which makes it a length-dependent decision rather than a general improvement over the transformers on a distribution pole.
claims.quote_verbatim: we're going to take some losses at the, at the transition from, you know, the, the high voltage point
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Line voltage can be read off the hardware: counting the skirts on an insulator gives roughly a kilovolt scale — six skirts suggests 66 kV, three suggests 33 kV — which is how a passer-by identifies what a given line is carrying.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of the tricks with insulators, if you count the number of rings, you can kind of get a rough idea of the voltage
claims.speaker: Toby Robb

claims.claim_text: Distribution steps down in stages: a zone substation per suburb takes 66 kV to 11 kV onto a bus, distribution breakers hanging off that bus feed the street, and pole-mounted or pad-mounted transformers make the final low voltage.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's when we take the 66 and there might be a couple of transformers hooked up to a bar
claims.speaker: Toby Robb

claims.claim_text: Substation measurement runs entirely on instrument transformers: a voltage transformer scales the bus voltage down to about a hundred volts, and a current transformer gives a proportional current at ratios such as 200 to 5 or 800 to 5.
claims.quote_verbatim: of those breakers will have a VT, a voltage transformer, which takes a proportion of the voltage and takes it down to about a hundred volts
claims.speaker: Toby Robb

claims.claim_text: Protection commissioning uses a programmable source good for a thousand volts at any frequency and current, with logic inputs to watch the result: wrapping its output through the current transformer several times multiplies the injected current, and the instrument times the breaker's contacts opening in milliseconds so the trip curves can be verified rather than assumed.
claims.quote_verbatim: wrap the output around the CT a few times to double up or quadruple up the current, inject some current and see if the breaker trips
claims.speaker: Toby Robb

claims.claim_text: Substations are built with standby capacity and bus-tie breakers so that a transformer locking out closes a tie and either brings in the spare or transfers the load onto the remaining units.
claims.quote_verbatim: if a transformer fails and locks out, the bus tie breaker might close and bring in the standby transformer
claims.speaker: Toby Robb

claims.claim_text: Power-line communication signals do not pass through a distribution transformer, so the network a given scheme can reach is bounded by the transformer rather than by the wiring — which is why the approach suits regions with large low-voltage networks per transformer.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of those signals don't travel through the transformer
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: The distribution transformer, not the individual inverter, sets how much a group of connected houses can export, which is the physical reason coordinating rooftop generation has to happen above the level of the house.
claims.quote_verbatim: the individual transformers will govern how much, say, a group of houses connected to that transformer can generate
claims.speaker: Paul Zawada
claims.episode_title: The Smart Grid with Paul Zawada

claims.claim_text: Large transformers have become genuinely hard to source, so a failure is a schedule problem measured in months rather than a purchase — and the usual fallback of buying from a large overseas supplier competes against that supplier's own domestic demand.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you blow out even a transformer these days, it's hard to source new transformers
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Grid infrastructure is physically vulnerable in a way that is rarely designed for: one 2013 attack deliberately destroyed seventeen large transformers at a single substation by targeting the mechanics rather than firing at random.
claims.quote_verbatim: destroying 17 of the substation's large transformers
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Mains hum from a transformer is mechanical: the laminations vibrate under the magnetic field when they are not bonded tightly enough or have lost their bonding, and the whole assembly can also vibrate against the chassis it is bolted to.
claims.quote_verbatim: you hear that 50 hertz hum from the transformer, that can be vibration in the laminate material
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: A transformer failure can propagate backwards: a secondary-side fuse clearing reflected back to the primary and pushed it into thermal runaway, which is the argument for protecting the primary rather than trusting secondary-side protection alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: the secondary side fuse actually popped. So maybe that had some kickback effect
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A transformer manufacturer will build a thermal fuse in line with the winding on request, set high enough that ordinary use and small surges never reach it; the trade is that it is a one-time device and the transformer is scrap once it operates.
claims.quote_verbatim: can ask your transformer manufacturer to include an inline embedded fuse
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: High-frequency noise passes straight through a mains transformer via the interwinding capacitance, so a linear supply is not automatically quiet at high frequency just because it has no switching stage.
claims.quote_verbatim: high frequency stuff will just go right, right through your transformer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Designing a transformer for a specific application — trading efficiency, cost and size simultaneously — is genuinely specialised knowledge that most electronics engineers do not have and rarely need, because off-the-shelf parts and complete converter modules cover the normal cases.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a pretty specialized knowledge actually designing, you know, a transformer for your custom app
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A mains-frequency transformer can be operated at other frequencies and voltages if it is derated appropriately, which makes a stock 50 or 60 Hz part usable well outside its nameplate conditions.
claims.quote_verbatim: using a 60 hertz transformer or a 50 hertz transformer at different frequencies and then the D rating you can do
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A transformer imposes no current limit of its own, and a fuse in the circuit does not make the secondary safe to touch — enough current passes before it clears to be lethal, which is what makes salvaged microwave oven transformers dangerous.
claims.quote_verbatim: transformers in general, you know, they're not current-limited. Even if you have a fuse in there, enough current can slip through to really mess you up
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In a linear supply the transformer and the enclosure carry most of the cost — a good 80-watt transformer is a substantial piece of iron — which is why a cost reduction on such a product almost always targets the magnetics first.
claims.quote_verbatim: most of the cost in something like this goes into, like, the transformer and the case
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Processors, CEOs & Soldering irons - Plentiful Perfunctory Programs

claims.claim_text: A planar transformer took several revisions with the manufacturer to meet specification, but ends up cheaper than a comparable quality custom-wound part as well as lighter — good transformers are not cheap, which is what makes the planar route worth the development effort.
claims.quote_verbatim: we are saving by going to this planar transformer
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Switching tens of thousands of times a second is what shrank the transformer, and with it the whole supply: the same power that needed a wall-wart in the 1980s now fits a phone charger the size of a cubic inch.
claims.quote_verbatim: these high frequencies, they can use a very tiny transformer
claims.speaker: Ken Shirriff

claims.claim_text: Inductors, transformers and antennas can all be formed from board traces, and they cost nothing beyond the area they occupy because the copper is being etched anyway.
claims.quote_verbatim: can do transformers on PCBs. You can do antennas on PCBs
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Wireless power transfer is inefficient for a structural reason rather than an engineering shortfall: the two coils are loosely coupled where a transformer's windings are tightly coupled, and the efficiency follows the coupling.
claims.quote_verbatim: wireless power transfers are inefficient because they're not coupled together
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: CAD courses and cross platform creation - Printing Propaedeutic Patterns

claims.claim_text: Treating a transformer as an inductor with a second winding coupled to it means an ordinary buck converter can drive one directly, which opens up isolated and multiple-output topologies without a dedicated controller.
claims.quote_verbatim: a transformer is just an inductor with another inductor coupled to it, you actually can use this as a
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Replacing a buck converter's inductor with a coupled one gets a second output for very little: the primary still functions as the buck inductor while a secondary tapped off it behaves like a flyback, giving two rails from one magnetic component.
claims.quote_verbatim: instead of using just an inductor, they're coupling that and using it as a transformer as well, which then gives you the flyback
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Isolated converters can regulate either through an optocoupler carrying feedback across the barrier or by primary-side sensing, where what the primary winding sees during the flyback interval is enough to drive the control loop — removing the optocoupler and its aging characteristics from the design.
claims.quote_verbatim: a couple now that have primary side sense
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Risky Components and Hardware Innovation - Slipshod Shack Shutdown

claims.claim_text: Measuring a converter's loop response rigorously means injecting a swept signal into the feedback divider through a small transformer and reading the result on a network analyser, which is what turns loop stability from an assumption into a measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put a little transformer into the feedback resistor network
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A half bridge ties the primary's midpoint between two DC-link capacitors so the winding sees half the link voltage, where a full bridge would apply all of it; the half bridge therefore trades higher primary current for lower switch voltage stress.
claims.quote_verbatim: the midpoint of the transformer on the primary side is into two caps
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: Multi-channel mains dimming needs an independent floating reference per channel, and neither answer scales: one DC-DC converter per channel becomes absurd at sixteen, and a custom switch-mode supply with one secondary winding per channel hits the same wall from the transformer side.
claims.quote_verbatim: don't really want to have 16 DC to DC converters
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A high-voltage supply can be built from a 10-to-1 transformer in a package a few millimetres across by treating one winding as a plain inductor — clamp it to ground while it charges from the low rail, release it, and the secondary delivers ten times the flyback voltage through a diode into a capacitor.
claims.quote_verbatim: you use one leg of the transformer and pretend it's an inductor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: At data-centre power levels the transformer, not the semiconductor, sets the topology: an 800-volt bus could in principle be switched down to 12 volts with a 1200-volt silicon carbide device, but only through a transformer too large to fit on the board, which is what forces the multi-stage conversion architecture instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: the answer is only if you have a transformer that big, which doesn't fit
claims.speaker: Alex Lidow
claims.episode_title: Inventing the Power MOSFET with Alex Lidow

claims.claim_text: Efficiency and spectral cleanliness trade directly against each other in power conversion: driving a clean sinusoid through a transformer with transistors held in their linear region can leave you around twenty percent efficient, while switching hard gets the efficiency back and produces harmonics to deal with instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you look at, like, a sinusoidal converter, right, where you're actually, you know, putting transistors in the linear region and actually driving a sinusoid through a transformer, you are burning tons of power
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Google Glass, Lean Startup and VotC - Initializing Instructed Interviews

claims.claim_text: The push-pull arrangement alternates two transistors to drive a transformer or inductor from a DC rail, and rectification on the far side gives a stepped-up or stepped-down output — the basic pattern behind most isolated converters, with dedicated controller chips available to drive the discrete devices.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can transfer power through a transformer or an inductor and then you can step it up, step it down, and then you can rectify it on the other side
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Digital isolators work by putting two coils between two dies inside one package — a transformer small enough to be part of the packaging — which is how isolated USB and similar interfaces are built without an optocoupler.
claims.quote_verbatim: they have two chips in there. And then, in between, they put two coils. And basically, it's a transformer
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A classic application-note thermocouple circuit sends data across an isolation barrier by driving one side of a transformer with logic gates, and it still holds up electrically — but with integrated parts now matching or beating that performance, reproducing it from discretes is hard to justify on a commercial design however instructive it is.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's got like a digital drive circuit with like some logic gates to drive one side of a transformer to send data
claims.speaker: Philip Salmony
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Transcranial magnetic stimulation is built as one half of a transformer with the body as the other: a current rising at roughly five thousand amps per second produces a field change fast enough to induce current locally in tissue.
claims.quote_verbatim: you basically got one half of a transformer. And you have something about 5,000 amps per second rise time
claims.speaker: Ben Krasnow
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ben Krasnow - Sprauncy Saccadic Spintherism

claims.claim_text: Inductive coupling through a barrier is usable at surprising distances — a through-window power link designed by an RF engineer works across about thirty centimetres of glass, far more than the millimetre-scale gaps people associate with the technique.
claims.quote_verbatim: he's just basically just passing power through a window up to 30 centimeters
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A commodity ATX supply is a cheap source of raw power for bench work: the 5-volt rail carries twenty to thirty amps, and boosting or push-pulling that through a transformer produces a bipolar rail at high current for a fraction of the cost of a laboratory supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: take a 5-volt, which has, like, 20 or 30 amps behind it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: A converter described as transformerless usually means only its main conversion path: a hybrid inverter still carries a transformer for the battery side, and every transformer is inherently bidirectional whether or not the datasheet says so.
claims.quote_verbatim: transformless if you just got that. But because this is a hybrid inverter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bidirectionality is exploitable: a salvaged distribution transformer run backwards steps a wall outlet up to hundreds of thousands of volts, which with a voltage multiplier behind it is how improvised high-voltage supplies are built.
claims.quote_verbatim: he used it in the opposite direction. So, you know, transformers work in both directions and he was stepping up voltage
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: China, Entrepreneurs and Blue Collar Reality

claims.claim_text: An induction motor can be modelled as a set of transformers whose secondary sweeps past the primary, coupling energy magnetically as it goes — which is also why the same machine recovers energy during regenerative braking rather than needing separate hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: the simplified model is basically, like, having three transformers and basically you're sweeping something past a transformer
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Specialized and/or Open Source Test Gear and Dev Boards - Vacation Videography Vorboten

claims.claim_text: Custom magnetics are where a nearly finished power product stalls: missing the efficiency target meant redesigning both the converter and its custom transformer, and that cost landed on top of a bill of materials that already looked too high for the market.
claims.quote_verbatim: have to redesign the custom transformer in it because we weren't meeting the efficiency targets
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

attribution_notes: attribution_reliable was not trusted. ep641 labels the guest's detailed account of substation practice as 'Chris Gammell'; the content is unambiguously the working power engineer and is attributed to Toby Robb.
ep220 similarly labels the guest's own anecdote with the host's name; no claims were taken from it.
ep539 (Big Clive), ep607 and ep71 carry the same single-speaker pattern; only unambiguous guest material was used.

One passage in the bundle carries episode: null and was dropped as uncitable. It contained the only material on on-chip interstage matching transformers at millimetre-wave frequencies, which is therefore absent from this article.
Reception, product enthusiasm and running jokes about the weight of large transformers were excluded.
